title: AI is being taught how to do your job. Will artificial intelligence replace us, or just change the way we work?
key_facts: Mercor, a multibillion-dollar firm, has more than 100,000 freelancers who teach AI models their fields; pay can range from $20 to $200 an hour.
Pew Research: nearly three-fourths of Americans fear AI is coming for their jobs.
A September McKinsey Global Institute report found AI could force 11 million US workers into new careers by 2035.
Economist Daron Acemoglu warns unemployment could triple within a decade in a worst case if nothing changes; he says AI-training jobs are small next to those replaced.
Stanford research shows hiring is down for young people in the most AI-exposed jobs; US Census research finds falling hiring and wages for recent graduates in AI-exposed majors.
Clara Shih, former Salesforce and Meta AI executive, quit in January and started a nonprofit to help young workers.
AI training is the fourth-fastest-growing US job category on LinkedIn.
quote_evidence: "AI cannot take the place of what's a fundamentally human business," said Columbus lawyer Kim Herlihy.
"What we are living through with AI is unprecedented," said Acemoglu.
why_it_matters_hint: Gives a mainstream look at the split between optimists and worriers about AI and jobs.
notes: Feature segment; relies partly on earlier McKinsey report.
